What this gives a session: after Claude edits a .go, .rs, .py or .vue file, Claude Code sends the buffer to `shared/tools/nx-polyglot-graph/lsp.mjs` and puts what comes back into the conversation. So a layer-, scope- or licence-violating import in those languages is caught at the edit, by the same `module-boundaries.config.mjs` table ESLint reads — instead of surviving until CI, or surviving CI, which for three of the four it does: ESLint has no parser for .go, .rs or .py, so those projects' tags have no mechanism behind them and their `lint` targets exit 0 over a violating import.

Why those four extensions and not .ts: the routed set is every extension the analyzer registry knows except the JS/TS family, and `src/lsp/editor-config.integration.test.mjs` in that project fails if this list and that registry ever disagree. JS and TS are left out because Claude Code gives ONE server per extension — the first registered wins and the rest never start — so claiming .ts would silently displace whichever TypeScript server the developer actually needs, to re-answer a question ESLint already answers. .vue falls on the claimed side of that line even though ESLint does read it: measured, a .vue file importing a banned package draws the same @nx/enforce-module-boundaries message from both engines, so Vue is the one extension both enforcers cover.

Node must be on PATH; nothing else is installed. Claude Code ignores manifest keys it does not know, which is where this note lives.

Bump `version` (here and in the marketplace entry, which must match — `src/conformance/plugin-catalogue.integration.test.mjs` fails when they drift) whenever THIS FILE changes: an installed plugin is cached per version, so an unbumped edit reaches nobody. Editing the server itself needs no bump: `args` points at the working tree, not at the cached copy. This version keys the manifest cache and is deliberately unrelated to the tool's own package.json version, which is what the server announces as `serverInfo`.
name: nx-polyglot-graph
description: Module-boundary diagnostics at edit time for Go, Rust, Python and Vue, from the workspace's own boundary config
